children: Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials), the consumer technology company, finally saw some improvement in App Store growth during September. The question is whether it can last.

App Store revenue increased 5% from a year earlier during the month, according to Sensor Tower data cited by UBS. That helped quarterly growth reach roughly 2%, an improvement from the flat pace seen earlier in the quarter.
Still, UBS analyst David Vogt is not calling it a turnaround.

The September quarter was Apple's second consecutive quarter of low-single-digit App Store growth, despite an easier year-over-year comparison. Quarterly growth also slowed by about 150 basis points from the previous period.
The U.S. and international markets each posted roughly 7% quarterly growth, although both slowed from the prior quarter.

For investors, September offers some encouragement because the App Store is an important part of Apple's services ecosystem. But the improvement arrived partly against easier comparisons, making the next few months more revealing.

October brings a roughly 180-basis-point tougher comparison and will be the first full month reflecting App Store changes in the European Union, which represents just over 10% of trailing 12-month App Store revenue.
Those October numbers should provide a better test of whether September was the beginning of a recovery or simply a better month.

title: Apple's App Store Rebounds, but UBS Is Not Ready to Call a Turnaround
